layers.title: Forest height
layers.description: Mean height of the forest canopy measured by NASA's GEDI laser instrument on the International Space Station, April 2019 to July 2025 (GEDI L3 Version 3). Fixed scale: 0 m is the bottom and 50 m or more is the top. Where GEDI has no measurement (mostly beyond about 52° N and S) the value comes from the NASA SVS 4950 visualization instead; the two are never blended. Taller forest sounds as a higher, fuller note. This is the fixed base layer.

source.title: GEDI L3 Gridded Land Surface Metrics V3 (NASA GEDI, ORNL DAAC), filled with NASA SVS 4950

layers.title: Wildfire smoke
layers.description: Fine particles (PM2.5) in the air near the ground, mostly smoke from fires, modelled hour by hour by NASA's GEOS-CF system for 1 September 2026, in the fire season. Fixed scale: 0 µg/m³ is the bottom and 150 µg/m³ or more is the top. More smoke makes the sound rougher and darker.

layers.title: Atmospheric CO2
layers.description: Carbon dioxide moving through the atmosphere from NASA's DYAMOND simulation with the GEOS model, over the whole planet. The timeline moves every region in 12 steps of six hours. NASA shows it as a turning globe, so no frame shows the whole planet at one moment: each side comes from its own stretch of the animation (Asia and Australia 14-17 January 2020, India 24-27 January, Africa and the Middle East 3-5 February, Europe and West Africa 12-15 February, the Americas and the Atlantic 23-25 February, western North America and the eastern Pacific 1-3 March); the Americas side decides alone around the Amazon, and elsewhere, where two sides meet, their dates are blended. It is the global context, not a measured effect of the Amazon. More CO2 makes the breathing pulse faster and heavier.

layers.title: Lightning
layers.description: Where lightning was seen from the International Space Station (NASA's LIS instrument), quarter by quarter from January 2017 to July 2023. Each frame shows only its own three months, nothing accumulated. Brighter means lightning in more of the ten-day windows of that quarter; it is a relative frequency read from a NASA visualization, not a flash count. LIS sees only between about 55° N and 55° S.

source.title: Lightning Events Detected from the ISS 2017-2023 (NASA SVS 5011)
